item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00285","case1_error":"Excludes Jose from the equal-sharing group, dividing by four instead of five.","case2_error":"Excludes Nicole from the oldest sister’s three younger sisters, averaging only two sisters’ clothing counts.","reason":"Both omit the focal person from a group that explicitly includes them, producing an incorrect divisor and group calculation.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00286","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2175 instead of 1975.","case2_error":"Omits the $400 food budget from total spending before calculating savings.","reason":"The first miscalculates a complete sum; the second uses an incomplete sum with correct arithmetic.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00287","case1_error":"Incorrectly simplifies 36 × 9 × 12 to 432 × 12; 36 × 9 is 324.","case2_error":"Evaluates 15 × 0.40 as 30 instead of 6.","reason":"Both write correct expressions and then numerically miscalculate a multiplication within them.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00288","case1_error":"Uses the old monthly salary for the new job, ignoring the stated 20% raise.","case2_error":"Subtracts interest instead of adding it and calculates it on the balance before payment.","reason":"Ignoring a required salary increase differs from reversing an interest charge and applying it to the wrong balance.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00289","case1_error":"Counts Reece’s ladder length once, omitting his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Evaluates 30000 × 4 as 12000 instead of 120000.","reason":"The first omits a required multiplicative factor; the second numerically miscalculates a correctly written multiplication.","judgment":"different"}]}
